headline: Samsung deletes health data if you refuse AI training
summary: A new option in Samsung Health allows users to opt out of AI training, but doing so will result in the deletion of all existing health data and cessation of future syncing. This policy impacts millions of Galaxy Watch and Samsung smartphone users.
details: Samsung Health has introduced a new setting allowing users to opt out of having their data used for AI model training. However, selecting this option triggers a warning that all existing Samsung Health data will be deleted, and future syncing will cease.

This policy directly affects millions of users who rely on Samsung Health with their Galaxy Watches and Samsung smartphones. The app collects sensitive information, including mental wellness, menstrual cycle data, and medication details.

Critics argue this move is anti-consumer, forcing users to choose between their data privacy and continued use of a service many have used for years. The company's stance effectively holds personal health information hostage.

While Samsung technically allows withdrawal of consent, it comes at the cost of losing access to one's own health history within the app. The warning also states data will be deleted "unless required by law," a phrase that has raised questions.

headline_marked: [[Anthropic starts localizing Claude pricing for India]], its second-largest market after the US
headline: Anthropic starts localizing Claude pricing for India, its second-largest market after the US
summary: Anthropic is now offering rupee-denominated subscriptions for its AI chatbot Claude in India, its second-largest market, though UPI payments are not yet supported.
details: Anthropic has begun localizing Claude's pricing in India, its largest market outside the U.S. This move aims to tailor offerings for the world's most populous nation. Local pricing has appeared on Claude's website and mobile apps for some Indian users.

India accounts for 5.8% of global Claude usage, making it the service's second-largest market. Previously, dollar pricing and currency conversion created friction for users. However, Anthropic has not yet enabled payments via India's widely used UPI network, unlike OpenAI's ChatGPT.

On Claude's website in India, Claude Pro is listed at ₹2,000 (about $21) monthly when billed annually, compared to $17 in the U.S. Claude Max starts at ₹11,999 (around $125) monthly, versus $100 in the U.S. Team plans are ₹2,399 (around $25) per seat monthly, compared to $20 in the U.S., with India prices including local taxes.

This pricing change reflects Anthropic's growing focus on India, following the opening of an office in Bengaluru in February and the appointment of Irina Ghose to lead its business in the country. Anthropic has also partnered with Indian IT services giants Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services.

This expansion faced a setback in June when Anthropic temporarily suspended access to its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for non-U.S. entities. While Fable 5 access has since been lifted, Mythos 5 remains limited. India remains a crucial market for AI companies, despite challenges in converting usage to paid subscriptions due to price sensitivity.
